## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by mottled tan to brown forewings, subtle darker lines, and a compact resting posture typical of many midget moths. In Florida, it is common and associated with warm open or semi-open habitats where grasses and crop plants occur, including fields, roadsides, agricultural edges, wetlands, and disturbed grassy areas. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are associated with sugarcane and other grassy plants, helping move grass and crop foliage into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
